# BAT-01: A sweep returns the same result for very different settings: the edit never reached the solver

## Symptoms
- A sweep is flat, or a 'robustness' batch shows no spread.

## Likely causes
- Missing or wrong `ModelFlags`: gravcomp and mass/inertia need `BODY_INERTIAL_PROPERTIES` (not `BODY_PROPERTIES`); armature `JOINT_DOF_INERTIAL_PROPERTIES`; gains, damping, friction, limits `JOINT_DOF_FORCE_PROPERTIES`; shape materials, gap, solimp `SHAPE_PROPERTIES`; equality solref `CONSTRAINT_PROPERTIES`.
- Construction-only: geom priority, condim, ctrl_source, joint_target_mode, solver options (cone, iterations, integrator, impratio). Never read by SolverMuJoCo: restitution, joint_velocity_limit, joint_enabled, body_inv_mass/inv_inertia; kf only with Newton contacts.
- Inactive mode (`mujoco.solref` outside RAW mode) or the wrong array (CTL-01).
- Only world 0 edited (BAT-02); a captured graph replays old pointers (BAT-04); reset/restore re-applied old values; the scenario setup never applied its perturbation.
- Your harness dropped the value (JSON int keys became str, a stale variable). Or the knob is real but irrelevant (CON-03).

## Checks
- Positive control: push an extreme value through the same path; the output must change grossly.
- `report_solver_params(solver, kind)` `pending` column (MCP `solver_params`); `solver.check_world_values(name)`.
- Read back the t=0 state of every world after scenario setup.

## Repairs
- Use the right flag, or rebuild the solver for construction-time fields and re-capture graphs; set values at build time in the script.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Drawing physical conclusions from a flat sweep; writing compiled `mjw_model` arrays as the fix.

# BAT-02: Multi-world batch: only world 0 changes, or worlds disagree with the single-world run

## Symptoms
- World 0 behaves like the single-world run; other worlds do not.

## Likely causes
- Label lookups (`list.index`, endswith) return world 0's entry; hard-coded ranges; actuator indices assumed equal to DOF indices.
- `control.joint_target_q` is coordinate-shaped when `newton.use_coord_layout_targets` is True (default): a FREE joint has 7 coordinates and 6 DOFs.
- With MuJoCo contacts, mesh/heightfield assets come from the first world; meshes authored in world coordinates bake one placement; worlds must have the same shape types in the same order.
- Tendon rows added with `add_custom_values` and no explicit `mujoco:tendon_world` stay in world 0 after `replicate()` (MJCF imports set it).

## Checks
- Twin test: N identical worlds with the same edit; `report_health(..., twins=True)`.
- Print edited arrays reshaped to (world_count, -1); compare `control.joint_target_q.shape` with `model.joint_coord_count` / `joint_dof_count`.
- Run each scene alone and inside the batch; `solver.check_world_values(name)`.

## Repairs
- Index with `model.joint_target_q_start`, `model.find_joint_coords/find_joint_dofs(pattern, world=w)`, or `newton.selection.WorldView` / `ArticulationView`.
- Set values in the builder before replication; meshes in shape-local coordinates, one mesh object per role; Newton contacts when geometry must differ per world; set tendon_world explicitly.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Debugging physics from a batch where most worlds never received commands.

# BAT-03: Each candidate costs a full rollout: evaluate candidates x scenarios as worlds of one model

## Symptoms
- Search is slow, serial, or done in a hand-written replica simulator.

## Likely causes
- Model, solver and graph rebuilt per candidate; one candidate per process.
- SciPy Nelder-Mead's default simplex is 5% of nonzero parameters and tiny for zeros, so offset parameterizations do not move.
- Very large batches exhaust memory; a tail-world failure above several thousand worlds was seen (cause unknown).

## Checks
- Time one evaluation and multiply by the planned count before launching.
- Score a subset alone and at the end of a big batch; error vs world index.

## Repairs
- `newton.utils.BatchRollout(build, N, solver=make_solver, dt=...)`: `view.set_attribute(name, model, values, labels=...)`, `reset`, `run(frames, record=...)`, or `evaluate(candidates, scenarios, frames=, setup=, score=, passed=)`; see docs/concepts/batched_evaluation.rst. `newton.selection.WorldView.set_attribute(..., solver)` checks per-world support.
- Cases whose setup writes a field the solver shares or reads only at construction (solver options, cone, condim) run in separate models automatically; pass `build=` for structural changes.
- Drive population or least-squares optimizers with whole batches; chunk at a few thousand worlds and check chunk invariance; pass an explicit `initial_simplex` to Nelder-Mead.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Surrogate replicas (CTL-07); fresh processes for search (keep them for the final check).

# BAT-04: Garbage, CUDA error 700, or silently lost steps after changing live solver objects or CUDA graphs

## Symptoms
- The run breaks or silently ignores changes after you modify live solver objects or graphs.

## Likely causes
- Graphs captured with old objects replay stale or freed pointers after swapping `example.solver`, re-capturing by hand, or writing compiled arrays.
- Construction-only fields changed on live objects (cone, iterations, integrator, condim, priority, substeps, buffer sizes).
- `simulate()` swaps `state_0`/`state_1` inside the capture; with an odd substep count per graph, graph buffers and Python references disagree.
- Scalar kernel arguments are frozen at capture; arrays are read at replay.

## Checks
- Same change in a fresh process, and eager (no graph).
- After N launches compare `solver.mjw_data.time` and the state with an uncaptured run; change a scalar and see whether the trajectory changes.
- `report_health` for runaway speed or zero contacts.

## Repairs
- Rebuild the Example/solver with the option passed in.
- Capture an even number of substeps, or copy the final state back into `state_0`; pass changeable values in device arrays; re-capture after changing captured scalars.
- MCP: `newton_rebuild` with `arguments={"restart": true}` recovers a broken process.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Calling private capture helpers; writing `mjw_model.opt.*` as a fix.

# BAT-05: Identical worlds or repeated runs disagree

## Symptoms
- Results that should be identical are not.

## Likely causes
- Unconverged constraint solves (frictionloss, limits, contacts) at the default iterations, so the warm start changes the result.
- GPU atomics accumulate in varying order; chaotic contact sequences (drops onto objects or rims) amplify tiny differences.
- Per-world contact overflow (CON-06); a perturbation applied twice or not at all (BAT-01).

## Checks
- Three in-process runs vs one fresh run.
- `report_health(..., twins=True)`; `stats["overflow_counts"]` for ITERATIONS/LS_ITERATIONS.
- Time of first divergence between twins; friction-off A/B.

## Repairs
- Raise `iterations`/`ls_iterations` until fresh and repeat agree.
- Treat chaotic outcomes statistically (rates over many copies and seeds) and design for margin.
- Use a deterministic mode (`SolverMuJoCo(deterministic=wp.DeterministicMode.RUN_TO_RUN)`, `CollisionPipeline(deterministic=True)`, `wp.config.deterministic`) only to debug single runs, after timing a short run (it compiles new kernels and can be much slower).

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Chasing bit-determinism; launching full batches in an untimed deterministic mode.

# BLD-01: Hand-built body: mass properties are wrong, outside physical bounds, or not what you set

## Symptoms
- Mass properties of a constructed body are implausible or ignored.

## Likely causes
- Wrong closed form: a solid ellipsoid has I_x = m(b^2+c^2)/5; a thin spherical shell has 5/3 of the solid sphere's inertia.
- Density on overlapping primitives counts the overlap twice.
- The builder adds shape mass and inertia after you set them unless `lock_inertia=True` or shapes have zero density.
- Reading a stale model after a rebuild, or the diagonal of a rotated tensor instead of principal values.

## Checks
- After finalize: `model.body_mass`, eigenvalues of `model.body_inertia`, `model.body_com`; `report_solver_params(solver, "body")` for compiled values.
- Ratios to solid and thin-shell inertias of the collider extents.

## Repairs
- `builder.add_body(..., mass=, inertia=, com=, lock_inertia=True)` with zero-density collision shapes; values well inside the band; re-check after every shape change. Docs: docs/concepts/mass_inertia.rst.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Tuning inertia to change settling or rolling behaviour.

# BLD-02: Compound or mesh collider: seams, gaps, wrong radius, flipped faces

## Symptoms
- The collider is not the shape you meant.

## Likely causes
- Strips approximating a curved outline overshoot corners or leave gaps; overlaps at different tilts form steps.
- Index or sign errors in a generator; reversed triangle winding.
- MuJoCo convex-hulls non-convex meshes; `Mesh(maxhullvert=...)` (default 64) drops vertices; separate convex sections leave seams.
- A new Mesh per world (slow builds); `ShapeConfig(density=np.float64(...))` raises the Warp 'mul ... vec3f, float64' error.

## Checks
- World-space corners/vertices of every piece: min/max z and distance outside the outline.
- Top-down labelled plot or render; drop-probe a grid of small spheres in one batch (rest heights reveal ridges and holes).
- Signed mesh volume > 0; collider radius at profile stations; shape type MESH vs CONVEX_MESH; build time for 1 vs N worlds.

## Repairs
- Pieces from a polygon clipped to the outline with one continuous top surface.
- One convex hull of a revolved profile with `maxhullvert` >= vertex count; overlap sections so no edge is exposed where contacts happen.
- Build each Mesh once and reuse it; cast config scalars with `float()`.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Tuning materials to hide a seam or gap.

# BLD-03: Calibrated camera: projected points miss the photo, or pixel-to-world placement is off

## Symptoms
- Image-derived geometry disagrees with known robot or fixture positions.

## Likely causes
- Frame conventions: Newton cameras look along local -Z with +Y up; an OpenCV optical frame is that frame rotated 180 deg about X; xyzw quaternions.
- Distortion direction (RealSense inverse Brown-Conrady maps distorted pixels to rays; OpenCV the opposite) and coefficient order (k1, k2, p1, p2, k3).
- A silhouette edge (object top, rim) unprojected onto the table plane; frame/sample index offsets.

## Checks
- Project known world points (robot base frames, FK of measured joints, fixtures) into the photo; a few pixels of error means a convention bug.
- Round trip pixel -> ray -> plane -> pixel within ~0.5 px.
- Render through the same intrinsics and overlay.

## Repairs
- `newton.sensors.SensorCamera.Intrinsics.from_camera_matrix(K, D, width=, height=, distortion_model=...)`, then `project`, `unproject`, `unproject_to_plane`, `compute_camera_rays`.
- Unproject each feature at its own height; keep a known-point validation in the analysis script.
- Fit the camera pose from keypoints by least squares before any render-loss refinement.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Adjusting focal length to absorb a pose error; pixel coordinates read by eye; trusting two fits made by the same method because they agree.

# BLD-04: Camera render: a shape is missing, visibility edits change nothing, or colours are off by a gamma

## Symptoms
- The render does not reflect the model you edited, or colours fit poorly.

## Likely causes
- Importers carry an rgba alpha of 0 into `shape_opacity`; collision-only shapes lack `ShapeFlags.VISIBLE`.
- The camera's shape BVH and enabled set are built at finalize; later flag, opacity or mesh edits are ignored until `model.bvh_build_shapes(state)`; poses need `model.bvh_refit_shapes(state)`.
- Back-face culling is on by default.
- `shape_color` is sRGB while shading and HDR output are linear; textures must be RGBA uint8 and `RenderConfig.enable_textures` is off by default.

## Checks
- Shape-index image (`create_shape_index_image_output`) at the expected pixels.
- `model.shape_opacity`, `model.shape_flags & VISIBLE`, and whether the index is among the first `model.bvh_shape_count_enabled` entries of `model.bvh_shape_enabled`.
- Render with `SensorCamera.RenderConfig(enable_backface_culling=False)`; the albedo output (`create_albedo_image_output`) should equal round(255*shape_color), as should a flat patch with ambient (1,1,1) and no lights.

## Repairs
- Set opacity and flags in the builder, or call `bvh_build_shapes` after edits; wind triangles counter-clockwise from outside.
- Fit colours in linear light with per-shape masks in a closed loop (2-3 damped iterations), then convert with `newton.utils.color_linear_to_srgb` / `color_srgb_to_linear` rather than hand-written formulas.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Judging colours by eye; changing light intensity to fix a colour-space error.

# BLD-05: Geometry edits (SDF, mesh) do not reach collision or rendering; probing contacts at a pose

## Symptoms
- Geometry changes do not show up where they should.

## Likely causes
- Collision samples the SDF data the model holds. A texture SDF from `Mesh.build_sdf` has a coarse grid plus fine bricks only in a narrow band; cells without fine data cannot be edited at fine resolution. Edits to a copy, or a rebuilt SDF that is not registered, do not reach collision.
- The rendered surface is a separately extracted isomesh; cameras only draw VISIBLE model shapes.
- Subtracting only the tool's current pose leaves material between frames; editing one level only.

## Checks
- Identity (`is`) between the SDF data the model references and the object you edit.
- Sample before and after at known inside/outside points with the sampler collision uses.
- Collide-only probe: set the pose in a state, `pipeline.collide(state, contacts)`, then `newton.eval_rigid_contact_kinematics` or a load sum; restore; compare with a fresh model.
- Removed volume by grid sampling vs the analytic swept volume.

## Repairs
- Edit in place on both levels; there is no public edit API, so isolate private-field access in one helper and prefer a public API if your version has one.
- Subtract the swept volume between consecutive poses; widen the band beforehand if edits go deeper; `SDF.extract_isomesh()` after edits; keep construction unedited.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Editing the render mesh; notify or pipeline rebuilds for in-place texture edits.

# CON-01: Contact parameters come from the other shape: priority, solmix and max rules

## Symptoms
- A held or resting object sinks into one partner, or slides, although its own material is stiff and rough.
- Edits to the object's (or support's) material have no effect on that pair.

## Likely causes
- The partner geom has higher `mujoco:geom_priority`: its solref, solimp, friction and condim alone define the contact.
- At equal priority, solref/solimp mix by `mujoco:geom_solmix` (min if a solref is negative); friction (per component) and condim take the larger of the two, so lowering one side does nothing. Both contact paths apply these rules.
- A soft robot-wide `default_shape_cfg` was inherited by fingers or feet.

## Checks
- `newton.utils.report_solver_params(solver, "geom", select=[...])` (MCP `solver_params("geom", ...)`): priority, solref, solimp, friction, condim of both sides. URDF shapes may be labelled `shape_N`: select via `model.shape_body`.
- Per-pair values the solver integrates: `solver_contacts(select, detail=True)` (MCP), or active rows of `solver.mjw_data.contact` (CON-07).
- Penetration per pair: `report_health(model, state, solver, penetration=d)["penetration"]` (pairs deeper than `d`, default 0.01 m) or MCP `contacts_between(a, b)`.

## Repairs
- Put the intended material on the deciding geom (or equalize priority).
- Build time: `builder.shape_material_ke/kd/mu[i]`, and `mujoco:*` custom attributes after `SolverMuJoCo.register_custom_attributes(builder)`. Live: assign `model.shape_material_*`, then `solver.notify_model_changed(newton.ModelFlags.SHAPE_PROPERTIES)`. Priority and condim are construction-only: rebuild the solver.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Stiffening the object that loses the priority contest.
- Raising mu when mu x total normal force already exceeds the load many times.

# CON-02: Contacts too soft, or stiffening does nothing: how shape ke/kd become MuJoCo solref

## Symptoms
- Penetration or rebound is off, and the stiffness you set does not behave like N/m.

## Likely causes
- The mapping depends on `model.mujoco.solref_mode` and the contact path. Builder shapes default to legacy MJCF_DEFAULT: unit-mass numerics `timeconst = 2/kd`, `dampratio = kd/(2*sqrt(ke))`, not N/m. Force-space mode scales by (1-dmax) and `body_invweight0`, only with Newton contacts (`use_mujoco_contacts=False`). `mujoco.solref` is used only in RAW mode.
- Impedance is acceleration-level: under a fixed push (a grip) one solref sinks a lighter body more; under its own weight the sink is mass-independent.
- `refsafe`: a positive timeconst below `2*dt` is evaluated as `2*dt`; stiffer gains then saturate.

## Checks
- `report_solver_params(solver, "geom", select)`: solref, solimp, solref_mode, `pending`.
- Effective N/m at a steady hold: normal force / penetration (MCP `contacts_between(a, b)`); compiled timeconst vs `2*dt`.
- Mass test, load fixed: sink halves under a fixed push (unchanged under own weight) for legacy contacts; force-space contacts sink by load/ke.

## Repairs
- Pick tau >= 2*dt (a few substeps) and zeta near 1 for resting contact; legacy mapping: `kd = 2/tau`, `ke = (kd/(2*zeta))**2`. Verify in the report.
- Impacts that barely rebound need an overdamped contact (zeta well above 1); bouncy impacts need zeta below 1. Sweep kd over a wide range (an order of magnitude or more each way), batched together with friction, before changing solvers.
- Stiffer than 2*dt allows: reduce dt; direct-format negative solref bypasses refsafe (test stability).
- For impacts, set the damping ratio from the measured rebound ratio (rebound energy falls as zeta rises).

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- `shape_material_restitution` is not read by SolverMuJoCo.
- Re-deriving the mapping from kernels.py: see docs/solvers/mujoco.rst (Contact solref conversion) and docs/concepts/simulation_tuning_mujoco.rst.

# CON-03: A firmly held object creeps slowly and no contact parameter moves it

## Symptoms
- A stiff grasp still slides along the pads at a constant slow rate; no rotation, fingers fixed to the hand.

## Likely causes
- Discretization floor of soft friction: friction rows act on velocity with a reference time constant clamped to 2*dt (refsafe), so slip scales with dt; it is not Coulomb slip.
- kf (read only with Newton contacts and the elliptic cone) saturates at the same clamp.
- Rule out CON-01 and CON-07 first.

## Checks
- Friction budget: mu x total normal force >> m(g+a).
- One batched one-at-a-time table: mu x2, kf x10 (where read), impratio x4, iterations x5, ke x4, dt/2. Only dt moves the creep: this card.
- Active rows of `solver.mjw_data.contact`: `solreffriction` (or `solref` where it is 0) below 2*dt means the clamp is active.

## Repairs
- More substeps if dt may change; keep the elliptic cone (CON-04).
- Empirical: lowering solimp dmin/dmax on the deciding geom in small steps reduced creep, at the cost of penetration and a cliff where the grip is lost.
- Otherwise report the residual and stop (harness lesson L02).

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- noslip: no SolverMuJoCo option; MuJoCo Warp raises `NotImplementedError: noslip solver not implemented`.
- Switching integrator: rk4 was worse and euler no better than implicitfast wherever tried.
- Collision every substep helps only with deep or soft contacts; ablate it.

# CON-04: Held object rotates or slips during motion: friction cone and impratio

## Symptoms
- In-hand rotation or slip under acceleration; a tail of copies drop the object.

## Likely causes
- SolverMuJoCo uses Newton's default cone (pyramidal) and MuJoCo's default impratio (1.0) unless the constructor or `model.mujoco` sets them. Pyramidal cones with soft friction rows slip more.
- Changing the cone changes the soft-contact model, not only the solver.
- No torsional friction about the grip axis (condim 3 on the deciding geom, CON-05), or too little normal force (CON-09).

## Checks
- `report_solver_params(solver, "option")`: cone and impratio (compiled as `opt.impratio_invsqrt`).
- A/B as separate models in one batch: `cone="elliptic"` with a moderate impratio vs pyramidal, all else fixed; measure slip and rotation in the pad frame.

## Repairs
- `SolverMuJoCo(model, cone="elliptic", impratio=...)` for grasps; options are construction-time, so rebuild.
- Re-run any low-friction negative control after switching (CON-10).
- Use pyramidal only for cost or convergence reasons, and then re-validate holds.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Raising mu while the friction budget is already large (see CON-03).
- Assuming either cone is always more stable: compare at fixed dt.

# CON-05: Torsional or rolling friction does nothing; released objects keep rolling

## Symptoms
- Spin or roll resistance edits are ignored, or released objects roll freely.

## Likely causes
- condim 3 (default) has only sliding friction; 4 adds torsional, 6 adds rolling. A contact takes condim from the higher-priority geom, else the larger of the two.
- condim and priority are read only at construction; live edits are ignored, and writing `mjw_model.geom_condim` breaks the solve.
- Torsional/rolling friction resists spin and roll, not translation.
- MuJoCo Warp warns at construction when a condim-6 geom has a friction component below 1e-5. Contacts clamp each component to at least 1e-5, but tiny coefficients with condim 6 (and the pyramidal cone) can still go NaN (CON-11).

## Checks
- `report_solver_params(solver, "geom")`: condim, priority, `friction_inactive`.
- Per contact: `solver.mjw_data.contact.dim` and the 5-component `friction`.
- Object velocity right after release (a moving release looks like rolling, see FIT-04).

## Repairs
- Set `custom_attributes={"mujoco:condim": 6}` (or 4) at build time on the deciding geoms, keep torsional/rolling friction >= 1e-5, rebuild the solver.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Adding condim to fix linear slip.
- Live writes to compiled condim.

# CON-06: Expected contacts are missing: objects pass through, fall through, launch, or one world misbehaves

## Symptoms
- Contacts you expect are absent or dropped; identical worlds behave differently.

## Likely causes
- Large detection gap: `ShapeConfig.gap=None` falls back to `builder.rigid_gap` (0.1 m default) and a pair's gap is the sum of both shapes' gaps, so nearby pieces overflow the buffers.
- `nconmax`/`njmax` too low (set by hand or sized from the initial state). nconmax is per world, but all worlds share one buffer of nconmax x world_count contacts; njmax limits each world.
- Filtered pairs: collision group 0 collides with nothing, equal negative groups never collide with each other, shapes without `ShapeFlags.COLLIDE_SHAPES`, explicit filter pairs, shapes on one body.

## Checks
- `report_health(model, state, solver)` (MCP: `health()`): `stats["overflow_counts"]`, `newton_contact_overflow`, `contacts_lost_per_world`, affected worlds.
- Gap per shape (`model.shape_gap`, report `gap` column); count contacts at rest before and after cutting the gap.
- `model.shape_collision_group` and `model.shape_flags` of the new shapes; apply the group rule to each pair.

## Repairs
- A gap of a few mm on small shapes (above the per-step travel of fast ones); nconmax/njmax with margin for the largest world count; re-check after adding shapes.
- Give each free body its own negative group, or a positive group shared with its partners.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Filtering 'warn' or 'Warp' lines out of logs: overflow is printed once per solver.
- Retuning stiffness or friction for a world that lost its contacts.

# CON-07: Contact force readouts are zero or implausible, or raw contact rows mislead

## Symptoms
- Force or parameter readouts contradict what the simulation visibly does.

## Likely causes
- `mjw_data.cfrc_ext` is filled only when MuJoCo's post-constraint RNE runs: force/acceleration sensors, `opt.run_rne_postconstraint`, or `model.request_state_attributes("body_qdd")` (or `body_parent_f`) before creating states.
- Raw rows include inactive speculative contacts (`dist` > includemargin, `efc_address == -1`) and other pairs.
- Deep penetration creates side or tip contacts with odd normals.

## Checks
- At rest, total vertical contact force should be about m*g.
- Keep only active rows of the pair of interest; map geoms with `solver.mjc_geom_to_newton_shape` and `model.shape_body`; print dist, solref, solimp, friction, dim and the efc force.
- Prefer the helpers: `contacts_between(a, b, detail=True)` and `solver_contacts(select, detail=True)` (MCP), `newton.sensors.SensorContact`, or `solver.update_contacts(contacts, state)` with MuJoCo contacts on MuJoCo Warp.

## Repairs
- Read forces through the solver's contact path and sanity-check totals before drawing conclusions.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Concluding 'the feet are unloaded' from a zero `cfrc_ext`.

# CON-08: Fingers close past the object with almost no force: the grasp never forms

## Symptoms
- The grasp never forms; only one pad touches at a time, or none.

## Likely causes
- The hand is not where the real or intended hand is: latency, gravity sag, soft gains (FIT-03). Most common in log replays.
- Object too small along the closing axis, off the closing line, or pads close above/below its equator.
- Contacts too compliant (CON-02) or a soft deciding geom (CON-01).
- Pair missing or filtered (CON-06); pinch force never builds (CON-09).

## Checks
- Pad pose in the object frame at the close command vs the recorded/intended pad pose (FK of measured joints). Centimetre offsets mean tracking.
- Both pads have active rows at closure: MCP `solver_contacts(select)`, or active rows of `solver.mjw_data.contact`.
- Pipeline distance vs geometric overlap from shape transforms; A/B `use_mujoco_contacts`.
- Simulated pad-to-pad distance during the hold vs the logged opening; stiffen contacts once as a test: if the shortfall stays, it is geometry.

## Repairs
- Fix arm tracking first; size the gripped dimension from the recorded opening and cross-check with images.
- Then stiffen contacts in force units and make the force limit bind.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Raising friction while the normal force is near zero; tuning contacts while the pads close in the wrong place.

# CON-09: Grip force or finger gap is wrong: the force limit never binds, or the finger-mirror equality yields

## Symptoms
- The gripper squeezes with the wrong force, or its fingers are not symmetric under load.

## Likely causes
- A position servo pushes `kp*(target-q) - kd*qd`; if kp times the remaining error is below the limit, the limit never binds.
- The limit sits in an array the solver does not read: JOINT_TARGET actuators (MJCF `<position>` imports) take the joint cap from `joint_effort_limit`; `mujoco.actuator_forcerange` applies only with `actuator_has_forcerange`, at construction.
- forcelimited without has_forcerange gives range (0, 0): 'invalid force range'.
- Equality constraints (finger mirror, loop closures) use a soft default solref, so the violation grows with force.

## Checks
- Per-pad normal force (MCP `contacts_between(object, pads, detail=True)`, or `SensorContact`) vs the limit; kp x (target - q_hold) vs the limit.
- `report_solver_params(solver, "actuator")`: compiled gainprm, forcerange, `from`, `joint_actfrcrange`.
- Mirror residual from both finger q; `report_solver_params(solver, "equality")` for eq_solref.

## Repairs
- Stiff enough servo so the limit saturates, limit = intended force, set where read (joint_effort_limit, or forcerange + has_forcerange + forcelimited at build), rebuild.
- Stiffen `model.mujoco.eq_solref` (tau >= 2*dt, zeta ~1), refresh with `CONSTRAINT_PROPERTIES`.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Editing actuator_gainprm/forcerange live for JOINT_TARGET actuators; copying gains into actuator attributes 'for consistency' (broke compilation).

# CON-10: A negative control holds: the object lifts with near-zero friction or an open gripper

## Symptoms
- A control that should fail passes, often only in some copies.

## Likely causes
- Squeeze x residual friction exceeds the weight: 2*mu*F >= m*g.
- Wedging or caging: non-parallel faces, pad bumps, multi-sphere necks, seams between convex pieces; soft contacts let geometry interlock; pads close off the equator.
- condim 6 torsional/rolling friction still acts; high impratio stiffens friction.
- A diverged copy is counted as held (CON-11), or the metric measures a different point than the criterion (tipping raises the centre).

## Checks
- Compute 2*mu*F/(m*g) for the control.
- At lift-off (MCP `contacts_between(object, None, detail=True)`, or `SensorContact`): normal vs tangential force, carrying shapes, upward normal components (wedge).
- Run controls on the full jittered ensemble with several seeds, in the same batch as the positive check.
- Track lowest point and orientation as well as the centre; check `state.body_q` is finite per copy.

## Repairs
- Stiffen normal contacts; one convex hull where fingers touch; smallest pinch force that still holds nominally; correct object size and grasp height; re-run controls after every geometry, material or solver change.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Moving the start pose so caging does not happen for your seeds; lowering rolling friction alone.

# CON-11: Some worlds go NaN or explode

## Symptoms
- A subset of worlds diverges while identical-looking worlds are fine.

## Likely causes
- MuJoCo Warp 3.14's Newton solver with the pyramidal cone, condim 6 and near-zero sliding friction (~0.002) returns NaN in the first steps, while MuJoCo C stays finite; CG and the elliptic cone stay finite.
- Tiny torsional/rolling friction with condim 6 (see the MJ_MINMU warning).
- Constraint buffer overflow; dropped rows destabilize the step (CON-06).
- Contacts too stiff for dt, or bodies starting in penetration.

## Checks
- `report_health(model, state, solver, per_world=True)`: non-finite worlds, runaway speed, overflow counts, deepest pairs.
- Batch A/B as separate models: elliptic vs pyramidal; `solver="cg"` vs `"newton"`.
- `solver.mjw_data.nefc` vs njmax; friction triples vs 1e-5; lowest point at t=0 vs the support.

## Repairs
- Elliptic cone; torsional/rolling >= 1e-5 with condim 6; explicit njmax/nconmax; lower dt or soften the unstable contact; stress-test with a large jittered batch.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Metrics that count a NaN copy as 'held' or 'placed'.
- Shipping extra iterations for a once-per-solver linesearch message without an A/B.

# CTL-01: Servo gain or target edits have no, partial or unexpected effect

## Symptoms
- Gain or target changes do not show up in the motion, or a moving reference lags by a constant phase.

## Likely causes
- Gains are compiled at construction and refreshed only by `solver.notify_model_changed(newton.ModelFlags.JOINT_DOF_FORCE_PROPERTIES)` (or the broader `JOINT_DOF_PROPERTIES`).
- JOINT_TARGET actuators (including MJCF `<position>`/`<velocity>` imports) read `model.joint_target_ke/kd`; `model.mujoco.actuator_gainprm/biasprm/forcerange` are ignored for them.
- POSITION mode is `gainprm=[kp]`, `biasprm=[0,-kp,-kd]`: damping pulls toward zero velocity and `joint_target_qd` is unused (only VELOCITY and POSITION_VELOCITY create a velocity actuator).
- A reset/restore re-applied old values, or only world 0 was edited (BAT-02).

## Checks
- `report_solver_params(solver, "actuator")`: compiled gainprm/biasprm, `from`, `pending`. Raw: `solver.mjw_model.actuator_gainprm`/`actuator_biasprm` via `solver.mjc_actuator_to_newton_idx`.
- `model.joint_target_mode` per DOF; `model.mujoco.ctrl_source`.
- One-joint step response at two gains.

## Repairs
- Write `joint_target_ke/kd` for every world, notify, and re-apply after any reset.
- Track a moving reference with a POSITION servo via the target offset `q* = q_ref + (kd*qd_ref + tau_ff)/kp`, or use POSITION_VELOCITY.
- Read docs/solvers/mujoco.rst: Actuators; Actuator gains and control source; Runtime updates.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Mirroring gains into `actuator_gainprm` 'for consistency'; treating writes to `solver.mjw_model` as a model edit (a later notify or a new solver overwrites them; use them only for per-step gain scheduling you own).

# CTL-02: Floating-base robot sags, sways and falls under joint-PD tracking; feedforward is fought by the servo

## Symptoms
- Whole-body sag and an under-damped sway about the ankles; or computed torques that the servo resists.

## Likely causes
- kp sized from rotor armature (a reflected-inertia frequency) rather than gravity load; kd sized the same way leaves the whole-body sway mode under-damped.
- Very high gains cause contact chatter and foot slip.
- Feedforward torque realized as a target offset once per control period while the servo's `kp*(q*-q) - kd*qd` acts every physics step; velocity feedforward missing; the effort limit clips the sum.

## Checks
- Static gravity torque per stance joint (`newton.eval_inverse_dynamics_passive`, or MuJoCo `qfrc_bias` at zero velocity) vs kp x tolerable error.
- Steady-state joint error and `solver.mjw_data.actuator_force` / limit.
- Sway period from root pitch; compare kd with body inertia about the ankle axis.
- Static hold with zero motion; actuator force vs planned torque over one control period.

## Repairs
- kp from load, kd near-critical for the body mode, per joint group; keep effort limits.
- Gravity/inverse-dynamics feedforward instead of extreme gains or integrators (CTL-04).
- Recompute target offsets every physics step, including kd*qd_ref; lower servo impedance where feedforward carries the load.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- One global gain sweep; joint integrators in double support.

# CTL-03: Joints track the reference but the robot tips or its feet spin: the reference is not dynamically feasible

## Symptoms
- The motion itself cannot be balanced by this robot; tracking it better makes it fall more reliably.

## Likely causes
- Retargeted clips lift heels, pivot or skate planted feet, float or sink soles.
- Reference ZMP/CoP leaves the support polygon; torque demands exceed effort limits.
- Small feet: little support area and friction moment; when the robot tips, feet unload and yaw friction collapses while stiff hip-yaw servos pass the turning torque.
- Linear interpolation of low-rate keyframes gives impulsive accelerations; finite differences amplify them.

## Checks
- FK the reference (`newton.eval_fk` on a scratch state): sole height and tilt per foot.
- Reference CoM/ZMP from smoothed CoM acceleration vs the support polygon of the foot colliders.
- Reference inverse dynamics (`newton.eval_inverse_dynamics_force` or `mujoco.mj_inverse`) vs `model.joint_effort_limit`.
- Per-foot normal force and yaw over a turn; required yaw moment vs mu*N*r.

## Repairs
- Make the plan feasible before tracking: flat-foot leg IK at planted poses, CoM/ZMP clamp with margin, smoothing (zero-lag Gaussian or spline, then differentiate), inverse-dynamics feedforward.
- Or a contact-constrained inverse-dynamics QP (friction cone, CoP limits) whose slack goes to unscored quantities.
- Soften hip yaw; low-pass unscored root yaw.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Stacking joint-space heuristics against an infeasible reference; editing the scored reference itself.

# CTL-04: A feedback channel destabilizes as soon as it is enabled, or integral action makes standing worse

## Symptoms
- Closing a loop makes things worse instead of better.

## Likely causes
- Sign or frame error: quaternion order (Newton xyzw vs MuJoCo wxyz), world vs body angular velocity, COM vs origin velocity (CTL-06); an unnormalized rotation axis.
- Positive feedback through targets computed from measured quantities the correction itself moves (measured foot anchors, toe-edge tipping).
- A frame of delay when feedback runs at the frame rate instead of the physics rate.
- Double support is a closed kinematic chain: leg integrators wind up against each other through the floor.

## Checks
- Per-channel impulse test at small gain: perturb and verify the correction opposes the perturbation.
- Unit-test the orientation-error function on known rotations.
- Feedback at frame rate vs per physics step.
- Ablate ki on a static hold; log left/right integrator states and foot slip.

## Repairs
- Derive feedback directions from a Jacobian or the model; normalize axes; anchor to fixed planted references; add foot-flattening feedback; run feedback every physics step.
- No leg joint integrators in double support: use model feedforward, or a task-space (CoM) integrator with anti-windup.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Deleting the channel or sweeping its sign instead of finding the bug.

# CTL-05: Hand-written IK or Jacobian diverges, blows up, or returns zeros

## Symptoms
- Inverse kinematics diverges near straight limbs or yields zero sensitivities.

## Likely causes
- Near-straight knees/elbows are singular; joint limits bind.
- `wp.array.numpy()` on a CPU array returns a view: a 'copy' taken before a perturbation aliases the perturbed data.
- Your FK disagrees with the simulator on joint order or quaternion convention.

## Checks
- Compare your FK with `newton.eval_fk` for the same `joint_q`.
- `np.shares_memory(a, b)` on arrays used in finite differences.
- Condition number at the reference pose; clamp against `model.joint_limit_lower/upper`.

## Repairs
- `newton.ik.IKSolver` with `IKObjectivePosition`, `IKObjectiveRotation`, `IKObjectiveJointLimit` (batched, limits), or `newton.eval_jacobian`.
- Damped least squares with task priorities (feet first); `.numpy().copy()`.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Finite differences on aliased arrays; undamped pseudo-inverses.

# CTL-06: Newton vs MuJoCo state conventions and names break a planner, estimator or feedback law

## Symptoms
- Conversions and lookups between Newton and the solver's MuJoCo model are subtly wrong.

## Likely causes
- Newton FREE joint: q = position + xyzw quaternion; qd = COM linear velocity and angular velocity, both in the parent (world) frame.
- MuJoCo free joint: qpos uses wxyz; qvel = body-origin linear velocity (world) and angular velocity in the body frame. Scalar joints: qpos = joint_q + `mujoco:dof_ref`.
- Compiled body and joint names are Newton labels with '/' replaced by '_' (a suffix on duplicates); geom names are '<shape label>_<shape index>'.
- A solver-built MjModel was not loaded from XML, so `mj_saveLastXML` has nothing to save.

## Checks
- Round-trip `solver.convert_joint_coords_to_mujoco(q, qd)` and `convert_joint_coords_from_mujoco(...)`.
- Compare `mj_forward` body poses with `newton.eval_fk`; run a rotated and translated copy of the motion.

## Repairs
- Use the converters (batched over time); never hand-reorder.
- `model.find_bodies(pattern)` + `solver.newton_body_to_mjc_body` (similar maps exist for shapes, joints, DOFs, actuators).
- XML: `SolverMuJoCo(model, save_to_mjcf=path)`; binary: `mujoco.mj_saveModel(solver.mj_model, path)`.
- Docs: docs/concepts/model_based_control.rst (coordinates, converting states, the solver's MuJoCo model).

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- `endswith` name matching; testing only at rest.

# CTL-07: Planner or private-model predictions diverge from the plant within one control period

## Symptoms
- One-step or one-period predictions differ from the plant by far more than numerical noise.

## Likely causes
- The planner takes one coarse step where the plant takes several fine steps with torque-limited servos and stiff contacts.
- The planning model's gains, force ranges or timestep differ from the plant's (the solver's `mj_model` keeps construction-time values; notify updates the Warp model only).
- State conversion errors (CTL-06).
- Finite differences straddle contact activation or actuator saturation.
- Hand-edited MuJoCo copies keep a stale `dof_invweight0` after mass/armature edits (call `mujoco.mj_setConst`); replica friction (tanh) differs from MuJoCo's frictionloss constraint.

## Checks
- From the same state and command, step planner and plant once; compare per coordinate. Repeat with planner step = plant step. Over a horizon, `newton.utils.compare_trajectories(plant, planner, tolerance=...)` gives divergence time and top contributors per signal.
- Planner vs plant `actuator_gainprm/biasprm/forcerange`.
- Predicted vs measured cost change for a small step; vary the FD epsilon.

## Repairs
- Plan at the plant step, or validate a coarser step first; copy commanded gains into the planning model.
- Smaller FD perturbations, smoothed contacts in the planning model only, regularization and line search, derivatives refreshed at contact changes.
- Prefer batched Newton rollouts (BAT-03) to replicas.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Validating a replica only where friction, damping and armature are zero.

# CTL-08: Controller holds a stance but fails at support changes, landings, or late in a cyclic motion

## Symptoms
- Contact switching, flight or momentum is where the controller breaks.

## Likely causes
- Instantaneous whole-body QP/inverse dynamics has no preview of contact changes or momentum; rigid point contacts vs soft contacts; soft (penalized) dynamics rows; support points on a tilted foot.
- Stance decided by foot height alone while swing feet move fast near the floor.
- Horizon shorter than the contact or momentum cycle; no CoM or terminal term.
- Sampling MPC: per-world inputs not reaching the worlds, noise scale vs cost temperature, too few knots, weights trading the wrong quantity, servos too soft for target sampling.

## Checks
- QP-planned accelerations vs plant accelerations; every force-carrying point actually in contact.
- Reference foot height and speed vs the schedule.
- Error per cycle at a horizon covering one full cycle; open-loop vs closed-loop replay.
- Spread of final states across sampling worlds; per-term cost of nominal vs best.

## Repairs
- Keep QPs for quasi-static balance; for stepping or jumping use preview control (iLQR on `solver.mj_model`, or sampling on batched plant copies with `newton.utils.BatchRollout`).
- Contact classification by speed and height with hysteresis; horizon >= one contact cycle; CoM/terminal costs; replan every period.
- Verify world spread before tuning noise, knots, horizon, iterations.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Writing a full QP/TSID before benchmarking batched sampling (harness lesson L06).

# CTL-09: Controller passes its own runs but fails a repeated, held-out or loaded run

## Symptoms
- The verdict is not stable across repeats, perturbations or machine load.

## Likely causes
- A marginal closed loop (contact discontinuities, thin CoP/ZMP margin) validated with one run per case.
- Wall-clock-adaptive logic tuned under the agent's own concurrent load; BLAS threads oversubscribed or limited after NumPy/SciPy import.
- Plans precomputed from construction-time parameters (frame rate, duration) go stale when those change.
- The delivered file differs from the tested one.

## Checks
- K repeats per case with perturbed starts, nearby rates and thread settings: pass fraction and margin.
- Compute per control step solo vs loaded (mean, max); `threadpoolctl.threadpool_info()`.
- Change the playback rate after construction vs resample before construction.
- Run the delivered file in a fresh process with the stated command.

## Repairs
- Remove the marginality (horizon, smoothing, margins); prefer settings with pass fraction 1.0.
- Deterministic compute with fixed margin, or load-probe scaling; thread limits before imports.
- Derive plans from the motion's time base on demand.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- One run per clip; timing measurements taken while other runs share the GPU.

# FIT-01: Identification fit is inconsistent or negative, or many parameter sets fit equally well

## Symptoms
- The fitted parameters are unstable or unphysical although the error looks acceptable.

## Likely causes
- Noise and filter lag in differentiated signals bias equation-error least squares; Coulomb friction switches sign near zero velocity; excitation too weak.
- Only base parameter combinations are identifiable; latency, damping, armature and offsets trade off; joints are coupled.
- Candidates mapping to invalid inertias are corrected at finalize with only a one-line count warning, so they are not what was scored.

## Checks
- Pooled vs per-recording fits; change the filter and see if coefficients move.
- Refit from two starts or on two splits; profile one parameter at a time.
- `builder.validate_inertia_detailed = True` during search.

## Repairs
- Use equation-error least squares only as an initial guess; then fit the scored output error (open-loop windows) in Newton, batched (BAT-03), e.g. `newton.utils.compare_trajectories(log, records, ...).objective()` per world.
- Parameterize so values are valid by construction; regularize toward nominal physical values; accept candidates on the total score only.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Hunting joint conventions once the pooled fit predicts torque; combining per-joint winners.

# FIT-02: Error plateaus at the same value under every variant: residual floor, missing mechanism, or reference bias

## Symptoms
- A residual that parameters do not move.

## Likely causes
- Unmodelled loads or conditions specific to one recording.
- Load-dependent gear friction (`fc + mu*|tau|`): constant Coulomb friction cannot fit slow and fast phases together.
- The reference is biased (tracker offset, in-hand offset): physics cannot remove it.
- Chaotic outcomes (impacts).

## Checks
- Correlate window error with torque, speed and episode; bin the residual by |tau|; compare holding torque with predicted gravity torque.
- Decompose: (sim hand - real FK hand) + (sim object - sim hand) - (reference - real FK hand); time-shift scan.
- Start-state consistency (measured qd vs dq/dt); per-trajectory percentiles; bootstrap at the evaluation size.

## Repairs
- Test one targeted mechanism and keep it only if held-out data improves, e.g. update `dof_frictionloss` per step from the applied torque in a SolverMuJoCo subclass.
- Otherwise down-weight or report the residual and stop.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Pushing unrelated parameters (gains, masses, geometry) to their bounds to absorb a measurement offset: it overfits one episode and fails unseen ones; refitting on the outlier alone.

# FIT-03: Replayed robot misses the recording: latency, gravity sag and servo gains

## Symptoms
- The simulated arm is stiffer, faster and better gravity-compensated than the real one.

## Likely causes
- Logged commands are leader targets; the real servo adds latency and finite stiffness.
- MJCF `gravcomp=1` removes a sag the real arm shows.
- Default gains and damping differ from the real controller.
- One global command delay applied to channels with different latencies (arm vs gripper).

## Checks
- Without simulation: sweep a zero-order-hold delay of the command vs measured q per joint; mean(measured - delayed command) vs gravity torque gives partial gravcomp; regress torque on (cmd(t-d) - q, qd, 1) for kp/kd; latency per channel.
- Then batch candidate (delay, kp, kd, gravcomp) sets as worlds (BAT-03) and score per-joint error with `newton.utils.compare_trajectories(log, records, times=, candidate_times=rollout.record_time)` (RMSE, divergence time, worst joints).

## Repairs
- Fit delay, per-joint gains, per-link partial gravcomp (`model.mujoco.gravcomp` + `BODY_INERTIAL_PROPERTIES`), armature and friction jointly on all episodes; hold one episode out.
- Set the delay to the faster channel and add the slower channel's lag through servo dynamics.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Raising gains to 'track better' (the real arm is soft and late); gravcomp edits with the wrong flag; world-0-only edits (BAT-02).

# FIT-04: Impacts, slides and rest poses do not match recordings

## Symptoms
- Where objects end up differs from the recording.

## Likely causes
- Friction not estimated from data; support height wrong (the lowest point of a rotated or multi-shape body is not centre minus radius); contact time constant/damping off (CON-02); restitution is not read by SolverMuJoCo.
- The release state differs (hand pose, velocity, gripper timing, pad drag): the most common placement cause.
- Bodies start in penetration or above the support.

## Checks
- Physics-first estimates: mu ~ a/g from flat sliding deceleration; support height = centre height - lowest-vertex offset at the measured orientation; damping from the rebound ratio.
- At release: simulated vs recorded hand pose, opening and object velocity; contacts at the stopping frame.
- Settle test with the robot away; lowest point per body at t=0.
- One batched one-at-a-time table; freeze the flat knobs.

## Repairs
- Calibrate support height and friction first, then sweep contact tau/zeta batched.
- Fix the release pose and timing before touching geometry; place objects at support height plus their lowest-point offset.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Inventing unobserved slopes, ridges or COM offsets to fit one episode; raising rims past the observed outline; torsional/rolling friction for translation errors.

# FIT-05: A calibration passes on the data you have but fails on unseen recordings

## Symptoms
- A fit that passes on all provided data fails on held-out cases by a small amount.
- Score differences between candidates are smaller than the spread between recordings.

## Likely causes
- Tuning on every provided case leaves no estimate of the error on new cases: the margin you see is optimistic.
- Fine grids (many digits) fit the noise of the sample, not the physics.
- Extra mechanisms (another solver, extra friction terms, offsets) add freedom that lowers the training error without improving prediction.

## Checks
- Split the provided cases (for example even and odd indices, or by recording): tune on one half and score the other. The gap between the two is your noise floor.
- Per-case error distribution: a few bad cases can dominate the mean; check which cases carry the error and whether held-out-like cases resemble them.
- Refit on the other split: parameters that move by more than their sweep step are not identified (FIT-01).

## Repairs
- Accept a candidate only on the held-out half, with a margin larger than the train/held-out gap; report both scores.
- Prefer a few physically meaningful parameters (damping ratio, friction, support height, delay) estimated from data over many tuned ones; stop refining below the noise floor.
- After choosing, refit on all data only if the held-out score stays within the margin.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Grids finer than the noise floor; switching solvers or adding mechanisms to recover the last few percent on training data; reporting the training score as the expected verification score.

# MSG-01: Quick reference: Newton, MuJoCo Warp and Warp messages and the card that explains each

## Symptoms
- A warning or exception text from Newton, SolverMuJoCo, MuJoCo Warp or Warp. Read the whole message first: many name the fix.

## Lookup
| message (substring) | meaning | card |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid force range for actuator` | forcelimited without has_forcerange | CON-09 |
| `broadphase overflow`, `contact overflow`, `constraint overflow in world`, `exceed the MuJoCo Warp contact buffer`; older: `exceeded MJWarp limit`, `nefc overflow`, `narrowphase overflow`, `nconmax overflow` | contacts or constraint rows dropped | CON-06 |
| `linesearch iteration(s) limit reached` | often harmless once; A/B before raising | CON-11 |
| `solver iteration(s) limit (iterations N) reached` | unconverged solve | BAT-05 |
| `< MJ_MINMU (1e-05) with condim=6` | near-zero torsional/rolling friction | CON-05 |
| `that their mujoco:condim leaves out` | friction component inactive | CON-05 |
| `requires homogeneous worlds` | worlds differ in shape/joint types or counts | BAT-02 |
| `Skipping joint entry N for tendon M` | tendon rows without mujoco:tendon_world before replicate() | BAT-02 |
| `Inertia validation corrected N bodies` | invalid inertia corrected at finalize | FIT-01 |
| `CUDA error 700`, `Failed to allocate` | stale graph or live-object reuse; batch too big | BAT-04 |
| `Couldn't find a function '<op>' compatible with the arguments` (Python scope); in kernels `Input types must be the same`, `Couldn't find function overload for`, `must have the same scalar type` | no implicit int-to-float or float64 promotion: write 2.0, wp.float32(x), float(x); from add_shape_*, a np.float64 config scalar | BLD-02 (config case) |
| `WarpCodegenTypeError`, `assigning to existing symbol` | kernel variable changes type; start with a float literal | - |
| `SolverNotifyFlags` | removed in 1.5: use `newton.ModelFlags` | CTL-01 |
| `Custom attribute 'mujoco:X' is not defined` | use `mujoco:condim`, `mujoco:geom_solimp`, `mujoco:geom_priority` after `SolverMuJoCo.register_custom_attributes` | CON-01 |
| `Invalid name`, `mj_name2id` -1, `No XML model loaded` | flattened compiled names; save with save_to_mjcf= or mj_saveModel | CTL-06 |
| `add_shape_box() takes 2 positional arguments` | only `body` is positional | - |
| `Specified texture channels do not match` | textures must be RGBA uint8 | BLD-04 |
| `NotImplementedError: noslip solver not implemented` | no noslip in MuJoCo Warp | CON-03 |
| `LinAlgError` | singular IK, or derivatives across contacts | CTL-05, CTL-07 |
| `joint_target_pos was removed` | use `joint_target_q` | - |

## Checks
- `newton.utils.report_health(model, state, solver)` (MCP `health()`) counts overflow and iteration-limit events per world; the solver prints each type only once.
- `inspect.signature(...)` and the docstring before retrying a call that raised TypeError/AttributeError.

## Pitfalls / shortcuts to avoid
- Grepping solver source before reading the message and the docstring; filtering 'warn' lines out of logs.
